walkthrough:
Rearrange and factorise the negative coefficient from the quadratic terms:
$$1 - 6x - x^2 = -(x^2 + 6x) + 1$$

Complete the square inside the bracket:
$$x^2 + 6x = (x + 3)^2 - 3^2 = (x + 3)^2 - 9$$

hints: Identify the reflection that turns $y = x^2$ into $y = -x^2$.
Identify the horizontal and vertical shifts to match $y = -(x + 3)^2 + 10$.
walkthrough:
Recognise that the graph of $y = x^2$ is first reflected in the $x$-axis to produce $y = -x^2$:
$$\text{Reflection in the } x\text{-axis}$$

Translate the reflected curve $y = -x^2$ to $y = 10 - (x + 3)^2 = -(x - (-3))^2 + 10$:
$$\text{Horizontal shift by } -3 \text{ units: } m = -3$$
$$\text{Vertical shift by } +10 \text{ units: } n = 10$$

State the transformation details:
$$\text{Reflection in the } x\text{-axis}, \quad \binom{m}{n} = \binom{-3}{10}$$
